target_chapter.title: Working with AI: from magic to engineering

canonical_support_green_reason: No separate canonical support test suite existed at capture time; original canonical hashes are retained as provenance only.
human_contract_origin: Earlier red-stage wording reconstructed from approved architecture; retained completion direction condensed from the current human instruction.
transcript_status: Condensed from actual tool logs with commands, raw stable outputs, exits, original action sequence, independent verdict, repair sequence, and accepted exact diff retained.
evidence_normalization: No timing or color normalization. Successful workers expose stable harness stdout; dependency stderr is included only on worker failure.
terminology_clarification: Final-polish terminology is application-visible fallback observability: Flask-Limiter owns transition detection and warning frequency, the logger assignment makes its record visible through app.logger, and historical receipt wording remains unchanged.
package_normalization: The final support copy replaces obsolete section and turn-by-turn comments in before, after, and top-level app.py. Final polish also replaces the same helper docstring in all three states with application-visible wording. Dependency hardening pins Flask-Limiter to the independently reviewed 4.1.1 runtime in the active package and before fixture. Runtime behavior, stable red and green output, and the accepted one-line production change are unchanged. Origin fixture and patch hashes are retained separately.
replay_dependency_scope: All replay inputs are inside the final Chapter 1 package. Original repository hashes are provenance records and are not resolved or verified at replay time.
approved_policy: Keep bounded fail-open overload protection and add one real fallback observability signal.
original_agent_selected_implementation: Invoke the existing application hook once per healthy-to-fallback transition through a Limiter subclass.
historical_repair_review_verdict: Replace the subclass with the smaller logger assignment and assert Flask-Limiter's existing healthy-to-fallback warning as the application-owned signal.
accepted_implementation: Assign limiter.logger = app.logger so Flask-Limiter's existing transition warning is emitted through the application logger.
human_owned_policy_boundary: Select the production monitoring backend and alert, recovery, and escalation thresholds.

independent_review.method: Read-only repository review using a clean disposable copy
independent_review.attribution_limit: Reviewer identity and tool version are package-attributed rather than cryptographically proven because raw vendor session logs are not retained.
